Canadian-founded, Palo Alto-based software startup Ollama has secured $65 million USD ($91 million CAD) in Series B funding to enable AI’s “personal computer moment.” The news: Ollama allows developers to download and run open-source large language models (LLMs) directly on their own computers and in the cloud.

The financing, which brings its total funding to $88 million USD, was led by new US investor Theory Ventures, with help from existing backers like US-based Benchmark and Y Combinator, Kitchener-Waterloo’s Garage Capital, and Vancouver-based GTMfund , among others.

Ollama, the Palo Alto-based developer platform for open-weight AI models, has raised a $65 million Series B led by Theory Ventures.
The round follows a $15 million Series A that Benchmark’s Peter Fenton led; Fenton now sits on Ollama’s board.

Ollama’s $88 million in total funding is a fraction of what its two closest comparables have raised, even as the company positions itself, in its own telling, as the largest developer network in the open-model ecosystem.

Concurrent with the acquisition, Tailwind Labs announced it is immediately closing new user registration for Tailwind Plus and ui.sh, effectively terminating its paid template business.

Key Elements Shopify Tailwind Labs Tailwind CSS Adam Wathan Tailwind Plus ui.sh MIT License Agentic Commerce Canadian e-commerce platform Shopify announced on September 9 that it has acquired Tailwind Labs, the company behind the open-source front-end framework Tailwind CSS.

What makes this deal unusual is that the acquired company simultaneously shut down the commercialization path of its paid products — Tailwind Plus and ui.sh will immediately stop accepting new user registrations.

A widely cited comment in the community cut to the heart of the matter: "AI and Tailwind-based template systems have essentially stolen Tailwind's lunch." One paying customer described their behavioral shift this way: "I bought Tailwind UI back in the day, and every time I built a product I'd browse through its components.
It buys Tailwind a few more years.

But like all these sugar-daddy acquisitions, the next step is probably 'Tailwind becomes independent again.'" Implications for the Developer Tools Ecosystem This acquisition reflects the deeper predicament facing open-source software business models in the AI era.

excerpts: $2 Billion Redis Labs CEO Says It's Aiming for an IPO Within a Year - Business Insider Business Insider Subscribe Newsletters Account icon Account icon Search Business Strategy Economy Finance Retail Advertising Careers Law Media Real Estate Small Business The Better Work Project Personal Finance Tech Science AI Enterprise Transportation Startups Innovation

Redis Labs, the startup behind the popular Redis database software, has surpassed a $2 billion valuation — about double the over $1 billion it was last valued at in August — as it prepares for an IPO as soon as this year.
That new valuation comes after Redis Labs announced Wednesday that it has closed a $110 million Series G round led by Tiger Global.

Those three firms also acquired additional ownership in the form of a $200 million secondary transaction, where they bought shares of Redis Labs from existing shareholders rather than the company itself.

Redis Labs is targeting an IPO that could come later this year or early next, depending on market conditions, and CEO Ofer Bengal says that the company has already started preparations — building on Bengal's previous comments to Insider that it was targeting 2021 to go public .
If a year from now, Redis Labs is at $155 million in annual recurring revenue, that would be a "good point to go public," Bengal said, although it doesn't see it as a strict prerequisite.

Bengal also said that Redis Labs was approached by several unnamed SPACs — special purpose acquisition companies, an increasingly popular financial vehicle that's allowed companies like OpenDoor and SoFi to go public without going through the traditional IPO process — to accelerate the process of hitting the public markets.

If not, we have the luxury to wait." Redis Labs says it's in it for the long haul Monday's announcement comes less than a year after Redis Labs announced its previous $100 million round of funding in August, at a valuation of over $1 billion.

Add to Preferred Sources In picking investors for its recent fundraising rounds, Bengal said that the startup went with the firms that could commit to sticking with Redis Labs even after an IPO, rather than dumping their shares as soon a they can.
